doc: ReadMe.md
---
What Kiwipow Agent is, what makes its workflow different from other VS Code coding agents, and how to install and start it.

- `#Why it's different`: a table of the product's distinguishing traits (code-blind feature planning, decision cards on conflicts, tests as proof of done, targeted verification, script-based tool turns, cleanup after green, compounding specs, docs evaluation) and the reason each exists
- `#Any model, per step`: the two engines (Claude Agent SDK, any OpenAI-compatible endpoint) and that a profile picks the model per step, with MCP servers, instruction files, skills and permission rules working the same on both
- `#Also`: the other session types and conveniences — chat sessions, Plan sessions, which tools and commands run unprompted, and querying large JSON by expression
- `#Get started`: installing from the Marketplace (Windows x64/arm64), the Anthropic API key or Claude Code login a Claude session needs, and the first feature-planning session
- `#More`: where to find the workflow, settings, build-from-source and intent docs

doc: docs/developing.md

How to build, run and package the extension from source, including the npm commands and the F5 development host.

- `#Use the working copy as the installed extension`: `npm run link-dev` to point the installed extension at the repo, what a reload keeps, and `npm run unlink-dev` to undo it
- `#Package`: the `npm run package` command and the `.vsix` it produces

doc: docs/intent/agent.md
---
The agent's definition: why planning is blind to the code, and what each phase, file, run and session is for across the whole feature pipeline.

- `#Why`: why the planner may not read the code — a planner that reads it inherits defects as requirements — and that phase 2 names disagreements rather than softening the spec
- `#Engines`: the two engines behind the single `CodeSession` interface, that a session's engine may change mid-flight, and how user and workspace `.mcp.json` servers reach both identically
- `#Shape`: the three phases, the file-on-disk state, the blindness boundary, the pipeline from docs and specs to passing tests, what an approved spec is, and that rules, tasks and decisions are named rather than given synthetic ids
- `#Stages`: the stage table derived from a feature's files, where spec and working files live and when working files are deleted, and what the plan bar and tab strip show at each stage
- `#Phase 1: Feature planning`: what the blind planner sees and never sees, its tools and denied Bash, the chat-direction-then-write flow, and the citation rules for rules derived from docs or specs
- `#The spec contract`: the required spec shape — reserved `Goal` and `Open questions`, one `##` per scenario, named rules with edges nested one level, no invariants or acceptance criteria — and that the extension parses every write and offers Repair
- `#get_work_item`: the read-only Azure DevOps tool: which fields are included and excluded, the traversal caps, the markdown snapshot, and why item state is excluded
- `#Docs split`: why all of `docs/**` and every spec is phase 1 scope while code and code-derived context is not, and the post-check listing of doc sections the spec now supersedes
- `#Finding the way in`: the docs map as the planner's entry point and citation source, reading markdown by section (outline for long files, MarkdownSearch with `path#Heading`), and the docs evaluation session that judges arrangement and then opens up
- `#Phase 2: Check against code`: the check's tools and inputs, that it is a run without a transcript of its own, what counts as a finding, the decisions file format, how the user rules in the wizard, and how rulings are applied, re-checked and turned into the task board
- `#The check has no voice`: that the check never asks and shows only a progress line, writing what it cannot settle as a finding
- `#Retrieval`: the `retrieve(question, known, budget)` sub-session that quotes without interpreting — derived tool set, no recursion, result shape, budgets, where results are written
- `#Phase 3: Implement`: the implementer's tools and inputs, one run per task and how runs are started and carried on, task states and the `ReadTasks`/`UpdateTask` board, proofs per rule as the evidence, and that only tested is a finish
- `#Unfiled decisions`: how a decision made outside planning is recorded — amending the spec within a task, or `plan/unfiled-decisions.md` — and the File decisions session that moves entries into specs and docs
- `#Migration`: what `Migrate plans` and Repair convert by rule, what is handed to the plan session to rearrange, rename following, and that approval survives migration
- `#Verification`: the model-free `kiwiAgent.verify` sweep over the files tasks name, how rules map globs and project markers to commands, where outcomes are recorded, and the failure budget
- `#Instructions`: the shared core plus per-phase instruction files, user and workspace instruction files on the own loop, and which rules belong in analyzers rather than the prompt
- `#Skills`: the skill folders under user profile and workspace, precedence on a shared name, how the index rides in the `Skill` tool, and which phases carry it
- `#Coordination`: the claim registry and PreToolUse claim hook, stale claims and force-release, opt-in checkpoints, and non-blocking session channels
- `#Observability`: what is recorded under `.agent/runs/<id>/` and that generated context (repo map, docs map) sits beside it with run logs
- `#Per-phase model`: that the active profile alone decides which model each step runs on, never per feature, and when a profile change takes effect
- `#Waiting for the person`: that a turn ending is itself the hand-back, and the status says waiting while the reason is read from the session
- `#What a session is offered`: that a phase's capabilities bound what the model can propose
- `#Parked`: deferred work (ADO work items and task write-back, repo map for phases 2 and 3, Anthropic Messages adapter, own-loop compaction, phase 1 retrieval)
- `#Interrupting`: that interrupting ends the current turn, abandons what was awaited, and the session learns how it ended on the next prompt

---
doc: docs/plan-sessions.md
---
The session types on the new-session screen and the feature-planning workflow step by step, from first prompt to verified build.

- `#Feature planning`: what the blind planning session may read and write, the spec contract it writes to, how rule names are used as anchors, and which writes are prompted
- `#Finding the way around the docs`: the docs map as the session's entry point and citation source, how it is built and rebuilt, and what the Evaluate docs session does and when it opens up to the full tool set
- `#The view`: the Plan/Chat bar and the Plan view stage by stage — Draft comments, Approve and the code check, ruling decisions, the derived task board and doc listing, implementation runs and the verify sweep — plus where the files live, when working files are deleted, and the Migrate plans command
- `#From a chat`: how a chat answers where a feature stands and writes draft specs from the docs when a project has no specs yet
- `#Unfiled decisions`: how decisions made outside planning reach the next planner, the `plan/unfiled-decisions.md` format, and the File decisions session on the Maintenance tab

---
doc: docs/settings.md
---
Every `kiwiAgent.*` setting and what it does — providers, profiles and per-step models, permissions, compaction, verification, docs map — plus instruction files, MCP servers and where logs go.

- `#Instruction files and skills`: which `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` paths and skill folders are read at user and workspace level on each engine, and how precedence works
- `#MCP servers`: how `.mcp.json` servers reach sessions on both engines and are named and allowed, the user-over-workspace merge, and the one-time copy of Claude Code's `~/.claude.json` servers
- `#Logs`: where session events, system prompts, generated context and a feature's working plan files are written under `.agent/`, and that it belongs in `.gitignore`
